question: How does a fine-tuned GPT-2 process an injected actor-name shortcut in IMDB sentiment classification, and can a head-decomposed token attribution method detect and mitigate that shortcut?

key_findings.claim: ActorCorr makes a small injected actor-label correlation behaviorally strong in the fine-tuned classifier.
key_findings.evidence: The paired test set replaces an original actor with a Good or Bad actor while preserving review text. Figure 3 reports anti-correlated accuracy change rising in magnitude from about 0.8 points at its smallest setting to 71.6 points at 1%, with the showcased setting producing a 33.14-point ACAC; purity 0.8 still produces an approximately 4-point effect.

key_findings.claim: Path patching localizes a mediated actor-name pathway from early MLP representations into a few late attention heads.
key_findings.evidence: For one Bad-actor/positive-review model, direct patching highlights heads 11.2, 10.10, and 10.6. Patching paths into those heads points chiefly to MLP 0, with additional later MLP contributions. Patching the proposed MLP0-to-three-head circuit into random-name inputs reconstructs 57% of the anti-correlated accuracy change and 69% of the correlated change, so it is a substantial but incomplete pathway.

key_findings.claim: Head-based Token Attribution is competitive with LIME on AUROC and separates known shortcut names more strongly by Cohen's d in this controlled benchmark.
key_findings.evidence: HTA sums, over selected heads, each source-position attention weight times the positive-versus-negative logit direction of that position after the head's value-output map. Figure 5 shows HTA and LIME with similar AUROC curves and HTA with the largest Cohen's d at the stronger shortcut frequencies; the paper also emphasizes one forward pass for HTA.

key_findings.claim: Ablating the selected late heads reduces shortcut sensitivity while largely preserving accuracy on original-name reviews, but it also removes useful correlated-case performance.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 reports ACAC falling from 30 to 6 and changes of only -0.3 and +0.6 points on original-name positive and negative reviews. The same ablation lowers accuracy by 8.3 points for positive reviews with Good actors and by 13.9 points for negative reviews with Bad actors, showing that the intervention suppresses the learned feature rather than selectively correcting only failures.

key_findings.claim: The experiments do not establish the paper's stronger claim that shortcut heads make a decision before the complete input is processed.
key_findings.evidence: The reported Label Heads write into the final label-token stream, whose query is computed after the full review prefix is available and can therefore condition attention on later context. Attention to an earlier actor position plus a label-direction output is evidence for an actor pathway, not evidence that subsequent context was bypassed. No context-swap, negation, or same-name/different-context intervention tests whether the head ignores later evidence, and the limitations explicitly concede that later layers or token streams may remove or negate label information.

key_findings.claim: HTA identifies a layerwise token stream carrying label information, not a causal contribution of the original input token.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 2 scores the residual representation at position i in layer l-1 after prior attention and MLP computation, so the representation can already contain information imported from earlier positions. The paper later acknowledges that HTA only locates the token stream containing class information and can, for example, highlight a final period that merely accumulated contextual information. Describing this as tracing a decision back to input tokens overstates what is decomposed.

key_findings.claim: The logit-decomposition argument omits GPT-2 layer normalization, so HTA is not shown to be an exact additive output-logit attribution.
key_findings.evidence: The formalization states that component activations can be projected directly through the unembedding and explicitly leaves layer normalization outside scope. GPT-2 applies normalization in the residual-to-logit path, and attention values are computed from normalized residual inputs; therefore LD(x at layer l-1 times W_VO) is not, as written, an exact contribution to the final logit difference. The causal patching results remain informative, but they do not validate the numerical faithfulness of Equation 2.

anchors.section: Appendix A.1 residual and attention equations

key_findings.claim: Shortcut-frequency and experiment-count reporting is internally inconsistent.
key_findings.evidence: The training split has 24,862 reviews, yet the main text calls 72 reviews 0.03%; 72/24,862 is about 0.29%, which matches the 0.3% point in the figures. Appendix A.2 says a setting of 0.01 corresponds to 24 reviews, although neither 0.01% nor 1% of 24,862 equals 24. Figure 5 calls the showcased model 0.003 while its axis is percent, and Appendix B.1 says there are 16 models although Table 5 lists five frequencies for four actor pairs, or 20 configurations.

key_findings.claim: The design does not isolate fine-tuning-induced shortcut learning from pre-existing actor-name associations in GPT-2.
key_findings.evidence: The shortcut tokens are real actor names and the counterfactuals are common random names matched only on gender and token count. The study reports no zero-injection model, no pre-fine-tuning measurement, and no permutation that reverses each actor's assigned sentiment across otherwise identical runs. Consequently, some name effect or localized entity pathway could predate ActorCorr even though increasing injected frequency strongly amplifies it.

anchors.section: Appendix A.2 actor list and injection

key_findings.claim: The shortcut-classification experiment is a known-span separability test, not automatic discovery of unknown shortcuts.
key_findings.evidence: Evaluation selects 1,000 positive reviews, constructs paired Bad-actor and random-actor versions, and reads each method's score specifically on the known name tokens. AUROC and Cohen's d therefore ask whether a prespecified shortcut actor span scores differently from a matched name span. The experiment does not search all tokens, aggregate candidates across a corpus, distinguish genuine from spurious predictive features, or evaluate unseen shortcut types.

key_findings.claim: The HTA comparison is under-specified and omits stronger shortcut-discovery baselines already discussed by the paper.
key_findings.evidence: Only LIME and Integrated Gradients are compared, despite related work on cross-corpus shortcut identification, feature-plus-instance attribution, and task-specific shortcut protocols. The HTA head threshold tau is never numerically specified; the Integrated Gradients baseline configuration is absent; Appendix A.3 says LIME uses 1,000 perturbations while the main text says 3,000 perturbed forward passes. These omissions prevent a clean compute and accuracy comparison.

key_findings.claim: Generalization and uncertainty evidence is insufficient for claims about LLM shortcuts broadly.
key_findings.evidence: All causal, detection, and mitigation results use GPT-2 on two-sentence IMDB windows and one injected feature family. Four actor-pair instances vary identity and gender, but there are no repeated training seeds per configuration, confidence intervals, numeric detector tables, larger models, other tasks, natural OOD sets, or held-out shortcut families. Appendix figures show that the most important heads change with frequency, actor, and category.

key_findings.claim: The proposed circuit is neither minimal nor complete, and the paper's own robustness appendix shows model-specific localization.
key_findings.evidence: Faithfulness transfers only 57-69% of the shortcut-related accuracy change, path patching implicates several MLP layers rather than only MLP0, and the top three late heads differ across shortcut frequencies and actor pairs. Head ablation can also trigger later-head compensation. A stronger circuit claim would require held-out causal sufficiency and comprehensiveness, random-circuit controls, and stability or alignment across trained models.

method.core_idea: Inject controlled actor-name correlations into movie-review sentiment data, causally localize the resulting GPT-2 pathway, and turn the discovered late-head computation into a token attribution score.
method.mechanism: ActorCorr replaces detected actor mentions with one Good or Bad actor under controlled frequency and purity. A GPT-2 classifier is fine-tuned to emit A/B label tokens. Random token-count- and gender-matched names provide counterfactual inputs for path patching. Per-head causal effects and logit directions identify late Label Heads and upstream MLP paths. HTA decomposes a chosen head into source attention weights and value-output logit directions, aggregates the token scores, and uses those scores for name-span separability and targeted head ablation.
assumptions: Actor identity is causally irrelevant to the review's true sentiment, so an injected actor-label correlation is a shortcut.
A common random name matched for gender and token count is an adequate counterfactual for the shortcut actor.
Direct projection through the unembedding is a useful component logit attribution even though layer normalization is omitted.
The high-impact MLP-to-head paths identified by patching describe the behavior rather than merely one redundant route through it.
Separating scores on known shortcut-name spans from matched name spans is informative about practical shortcut detection.
Ablating late Label Heads removes shortcut reliance without materially damaging unrelated classification behavior.

techniques.role: Creates paired movie-review inputs with actor-label shortcut frequency and purity under experimental control.
Measures the accuracy loss caused by inserting a shortcut from the opposite sentiment class.
Causally traces random-name versus shortcut-name activation differences through individual MLPs and attention-head key/value paths.
Projects component activations onto the A-versus-B label direction to identify label-moving heads.
Combines attention weights with per-position value-output label directions to score source token streams.
Tests whether disabling selected Label Heads reduces behavioral shortcut sensitivity.

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 fine-tuned on 24,862 two-sentence IMDB training reviews with four Good/Bad actor pairs and varying shortcut frequency and purity
evaluations.metric: Per-class accuracy and Anti-Correlated Accuracy Change
evaluations.result: Shortcut impact grows sharply with frequency; the showcased model reaches 33.14-point ACAC, and a nominal 1% setting makes almost every anti-correlated example fail.
evaluations.baseline: The same review with its original actor name, plus correlated versus anti-correlated actor replacements.

evaluations.setting: One Bad-actor/positive-review GPT-2 instance with 200 paired shortcut/random-name examples
evaluations.metric: Output logit-difference change under direct and mediated path patching
evaluations.result: Late heads 11.2, 10.10, and 10.6 dominate direct effects, while MLP0 and several other MLPs dominate paths into those heads.
evaluations.baseline: Matched common random names with the same gender and token count.

evaluations.setting: Proposed MLP0-to-three-Label-Head circuit patched from shortcut into random-name inputs
evaluations.result: The path reconstructs 57% of the anti-correlated effect and 69% of the correlated effect.

evaluations.setting: Four actor-name instances, each using 1,000 positive reviews in paired Bad-actor and random-name versions across five reported shortcut strengths
evaluations.metric: AUROC and Cohen's d of maximum or summed known-name-span attribution scores
evaluations.result: HTA and LIME have similar AUROC; HTA has stronger Cohen's d at moderate and high shortcut frequency, while Integrated Gradients is generally weaker.
evaluations.baseline: LIME and Integrated Gradients under maximum and sum subtoken aggregation.

evaluations.setting: Targeted Label-Head ablation and qualitative attribution on reviews without injected shortcut names
evaluations.metric: ACAC, subgroup accuracy, VADER top-word recovery, highest-scoring subtoken position, and attribution entropy
evaluations.result: Ablation reduces ACAC from 30 to 6 with small original-name changes; HTA finds 29 VADER words, matches LIME's count, and yields lower entropy but only small shifts in token-position statistics.
evaluations.baseline: The unablated model, LIME, and Integrated Gradients.

limitations: The study covers one small decoder model, one dataset, one binary task, and one lexical shortcut family.
Real actor names can carry pretrained semantic associations; no zero-injection or label-permutation control isolates those priors.
The main frequency labels and review counts disagree, and the stated number of trained models disagrees with Table 5.
Random-name counterfactuals match gender and token count but not frequency, familiarity, ethnicity, morphology, or pretrained representation.
HTA evaluates prespecified actor spans rather than discovering unknown shortcut candidates across a corpus.
The layer-normalization omission prevents Equation 2 from being an exact output-logit decomposition for GPT-2.
The selected head threshold, Integrated Gradients details, and LIME forward-pass count are not reproducibly reported.
No detector uncertainty, repeated training seeds, statistical tests, or numerical result table accompanies Figure 5.
The circuit faithfulness recovery is partial and the selected heads vary across trained configurations.
Head ablation trades away performance on correlated groups and is not evaluated under broad distribution shift.
The premature-decision interpretation is not tested against context-sensitive gating at the final query position.
The qualitative non-injected analysis relies on a small sentiment lexicon and selected examples rather than a ground-truth shortcut benchmark.
failure_modes: HTA can highlight a token position that merely stores information imported from other positions, producing a misleading input-level explanation.
A head with a strong label-direction output can still be contextually gated by its query, so attention to a shortcut token need not imply context bypass.
Final layer normalization can change component directions and scales, invalidating raw unembedding-based attribution rankings.
A random replacement name can alter lexical familiarity or entity semantics, confounding patching effects with the intended learned shortcut.
Distributed or polysemantic shortcut representations will not be removed by ablating a few high-impact heads.
Hydra-style compensation can move the behavior into later heads after ablation or further fine-tuning.
A threshold calibrated on known actor names may fail for multi-token, syntactic, conceptual, or contextual shortcuts.
At low injected frequency, shortcut and random-name score distributions overlap and the localized circuit becomes more diffuse.
Matched-token-length replacement does not guarantee equivalent token identities, position effects, or grammatical coherence.
An intervention that lowers ACAC can appear successful by degrading use of the feature in both correlated and anti-correlated groups rather than restoring contextual reasoning.
reusable_insights: Pair behavioral counterfactuals with internal interventions: neither attribution scores nor performance shifts alone identify a mechanism.
Report circuit sufficiency, comprehensiveness, necessity, random-circuit controls, and stability across seeds as separate quantities.
Distinguish an original-token attribution from attribution to a later residual-stream position that may already aggregate context.
Account explicitly for layer normalization when translating residual components into output-logit contributions.
Use real-language shortcuts for ecological plausibility, but cross them with synthetic tokens and permuted label assignments to isolate pretrained priors.
Evaluate unknown-shortcut discovery by scanning and aggregating all candidate features, not only scoring known injected spans.
Use held-out shortcut types, tasks, model sizes, and natural OOD sets before generalizing a mitigation claim.
Track correlated-group loss as well as anti-correlated-group gain so feature deletion is not mistaken for selective repair.
Separate parameter fractions from percentages and publish exact per-group counts for every data-generation setting.
Compare mechanistic attribution against task-specific artifact detectors and feature-plus-instance methods, not only generic salience baselines.
open_questions: Do the same late-head pathways emerge when actor-label assignments are reversed or when synthetic names have no pretrained semantics?
Does a Label Head still attend to the actor when later text explicitly negates or contradicts the actor-associated sentiment?
How much of HTA's ranking survives a layer-normalization-corrected decomposition or causal token-level resampling test?
Can an automatic corpus-level version of HTA discover the actor tokens without being given name spans or shortcut labels?
Are MLP0 and the late heads causally necessary and sufficient on held-out samples, or are they one of several redundant routes?
Can circuits be aligned across seeds, actors, frequencies, larger GPT variants, and instruction-tuned models?
Would retraining or editing the upstream actor representation outperform head ablation without hurting correlated cases?
How does HTA compare with training-feature attribution, cross-corpus stability, human-attention guidance, and robust-attribution training on the same benchmark?
What happens for contextual shortcuts whose spuriousness depends on syntax or negation rather than a fixed token identity?
Can uncertainty-calibrated shortcut scores predict real worst-group or OOD failures rather than only injected-name separability?

competitive_landscape.title: "Will You Find These Shortcuts?" A Protocol for Evaluating the Faithfulness of Input Salience Methods for Text Classification
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest predecessor for evaluating token-attribution methods with partially synthetic, known-ground-truth shortcuts in text classification.
competitive_landscape.difference: Bastings et al. test four salience-method classes across multiple datasets, models, and shortcut structures and show strong task/configuration dependence. The reviewed paper adds causal circuit localization and HTA, but its single shortcut family and known-span AUROC do not implement the predecessor's broader faithfulness protocol.

competitive_landscape.title: Combining Feature and Instance Attribution to Detect Artifacts
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct artifact-discovery alternative that combines token salience with influential training instances.
competitive_landscape.difference: Pezeshkpour et al. search for both known and previously unknown artifacts across several NLP datasets and include a user study. HTA is much cheaper and gives an internal head-level story, but it does not connect a suspicious test token to the training examples that induced it or demonstrate unknown artifact discovery.

competitive_landscape.title: Identifying and Mitigating Spurious Correlations for Improving Robustness in NLP Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct automatic shortcut-identification and mitigation baseline for NLP classifiers.
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. combine importance extraction, cross-corpus stability, and knowledge-aware perturbations to separate genuine from spurious tokens at scale. The reviewed paper gives a more granular causal pathway but evaluates only prespecified actor spans and therefore does not match the earlier system's discovery scope.

competitive_landscape.title: HuaSLIM: Human Attention Motivated Shortcut Learning Identification and Mitigation for Large Language models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Token-level shortcut identification and mitigation using human and model attention.
competitive_landscape.difference: HuaSLIM evaluates multiple NLP tasks and improves OOD robustness through human-guided self-distillation. HTA avoids human attention labels and supports a causal post-hoc intervention, but has substantially narrower model, task, and OOD evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: Explore Spurious Correlations at the Concept Level in Language Models for Text Classification
competitive_landscape.relationship: Extends shortcut detection beyond individual tokens to latent concepts under fine-tuning and in-context learning.
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhou et al. label concept bias and mitigate it with generated counterfactual rebalancing across broader settings. The reviewed paper is more mechanistic at the component level, but actor-name HTA cannot yet identify distributed or contextual concepts.

competitive_landscape.title: How do Large Language Models Learn In-Context? Query and Key Matrices of In-Context Heads are Two Towers for Metric Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Close pre-existing mechanistic analysis of label-moving attention heads in sentence classification.
competitive_landscape.difference: Yu and Ananiadou already identify a small set of important heads, decompose value-output label information and query-key routing, and intervene on label biases across five tasks and two larger model families. The reviewed paper applies related decomposition and causal patching specifically to fine-tuned shortcuts and derives HTA, but does not cite this especially close 2024 predecessor.

competitive_landscape.title: Exploring and Mitigating Shortcut Learning for Generative Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Broader study of feature-label-task shortcuts and mitigation in generative LLM prompting.
competitive_landscape.difference: Sun et al. study task-feature-label correlations across three generative tasks and use in-context information to mitigate them. The reviewed paper offers finer internal causal evidence but only for a fine-tuned GPT-2 classifier and a fixed lexical feature.

competitive_landscape.title: An XAI-based Analysis of Shortcut Learning in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Near-concurrent component-level study of where spurious features are encoded and whether post-hoc pruning assumptions hold.
competitive_landscape.difference: Le et al. define a neuron spurious score and compare entanglement in CNNs and vision transformers, finding that shortcut information can be distributed and pruning can remove core features too. The reviewed paper supplies stronger text-specific causal paths, while the cross-architecture result warns against generalizing its few-head ablation story.

competitive_landscape.title: Model Guidance via Robust Feature Attribution
competitive_landscape.relationship: Post-publication state-of-the-art competitor for explanation-guided shortcut mitigation, including NLP.
competitive_landscape.difference: Ghitu et al. optimize a theoretically motivated robust attribution objective during training and report broad gains over prior guidance methods. HTA is a cheaper post-hoc diagnostic and intervention, but lacks robust-attribution guarantees and broad benchmark comparisons.

competitive_landscape.title: Pruning the Paradox: How CLIP's Most Informative Heads Enhance Performance While Amplifying Bias
competitive_landscape.relationship: Post-publication attention-head analysis connecting useful concepts, spurious correlations, bias, and pruning.
competitive_landscape.difference: Madasu et al. use a concept-consistency score and soft-pruning across CLIP applications, showing that highly informative heads can simultaneously support OOD performance and amplify bias. This broader trade-off mirrors the reviewed paper's correlated-group losses after ablation and motivates explicit capability-versus-shortcut accounting.

competitive_landscape.title: Causally Grounded Mechanistic Interpretability for LLMs with Faithful Natural-Language Explanations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later circuit-attribution work that evaluates causal-head explanations with explicit faithfulness metrics.
competitive_landscape.difference: Mahale adapts sufficiency and comprehensiveness to circuit explanations and finds high sufficiency but low comprehensiveness because of distributed backups. The reviewed paper's 57-69% reconstruction and compensation caveat point to the same issue, but it does not quantify both axes or test random circuit controls.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims to move from behavioral shortcut identification to the mechanism that processes a shortcut, and introduces Head-based Token Attribution as a new efficient detector and mitigation guide.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Pages 1-2 frame prior work as identifying influential input elements; pages 5-8 localize an early-MLP/late-head pathway, define HTA, compare it with LIME and Integrated Gradients, and ablate the selected heads.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The controlled ActorCorr-to-causal-path-to-HTA combination is a useful and plausibly novel case study. Novelty is moderate rather than field-defining: synthetic shortcut attribution protocols, automatic artifact detectors, and label-moving head decompositions already existed, including a close uncited 2024 classification-head study. The evidence supports a GPT-2 actor-name pathway and an efficient known-span score, not the broader claims of automatic shortcut detection, context bypass, or a general LLM mechanism.

reviewer_notes: Read all 21 cached pages, including equations, Figure 3 and Figure 5 values, all tables, qualitative examples, and Appendix B path-patching figures. Competitors were checked against arXiv, ACL Anthology, OpenReview/TMLR, or official proceedings through 2026-08-23. The released repository was inspected only as a reproducibility cross-check; paper-level findings above are anchored to the archived PDF.
